info.text: Unit 23 — Loading and verifying avionics software. Listening, reading, use of English and vocabulary.

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 1 again (Starting the load).

The technicians confirm that the unit is at hardware mod 5, so it meets the minimum standard for this load.

True or false?

generalfeedback.text: The AMM task asks for mod 4 or later. B inspects the unit and reports mod 5, so it is compatible. A higher mod number still meets a "mod 4 or later" minimum.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct. Mod 5 is later than the mod 4 minimum, so the load may go ahead.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Listen again: B says "it is mod 5, so we are compatible". Mod 5 satisfies the mod 4 minimum.

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 1 again.

Why must the team confirm compatibility before they start the load?

generalfeedback.text: A (the lead) says the software "runs on one hardware standard only". If the hardware mod is wrong, the load will not run correctly, so compatibility is checked first.

answer.text: The software runs on one hardware standard only.

feedback.text: Correct — that is exactly A's reason.

answer.text: The load media is always the wrong revision here.

feedback.text: No. The media matched the card; compatibility is about hardware, not media.

answer.text: The dataloader needs a second green link light.

feedback.text: No. One steady green link is enough; this is not the reason.

answer.text: The tech log must be signed before any load.

feedback.text: No. The tech log is completed after verification, not before the load.

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 1 again.

Just after B presses start, at what percentage does B report the load is running? Write the number only.

generalfeedback.text: B says: "Currently loading at four percent." The answer is 4.

feedback.text: Correct — "loading at four percent".
The bar is already advancing. B reports four percent, not zero.

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 1 again.

Every how many seconds does B agree to announce the percentage? Write the number only.

generalfeedback.text: B says: "I will announce the percentage every twenty seconds." The answer is 20.

feedback.text: Correct — every twenty seconds.
Ten seconds is the wait in Dialogue 2 before the loader is switched on. Here it is twenty.

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 2 again (A failed load).

At what percentage did the first load stop and freeze? Write the number only.

generalfeedback.text: A says B "went quiet at sixty percent", and the bar is frozen there. The answer is 60.

feedback.text: Correct — it stopped at sixty percent.
One hundred percent is the completed bar in Dialogue 3. The failure was at sixty.

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 2 again.

How many seconds does B wait before switching the loader on again? Write the number only.

generalfeedback.text: B says: "I will wait ten seconds, then switch it on again." The answer is 10.

feedback.text: Correct — a ten-second wait during the power cycle.
Twenty seconds was the announcement interval in Dialogue 1. The power-cycle wait is ten.

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 2 again.

After the clean abort, the unit lost its previous software and was left empty.

True or false?

generalfeedback.text: B says the unit "has retained its previous software", and A adds that a clean abort protects the existing configuration. So the statement is false.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: No. A clean abort protects the old software; the unit was not left empty.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Correct. The unit kept its previous software after the abort.

name.text: L8 · Dialogue 2 · cause of the first failure

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 2 again.

Once the retry passes, what does A say the real cause of the first failure was?

generalfeedback.text: After the second checksum reads correctly, A concludes: "That was a defective card, not a bad file." The load media was faulty, not the software file.

answer.text: A defective card, not the file.

feedback.text: Correct — A says it was a defective card.

answer.text: A wrong LRU part number on the unit.

feedback.text: No. The part number was never in doubt in this dialogue.

answer.text: An out-of-date revision of the software file.

feedback.text: No. The file was fine; the same file loaded from a good card.

answer.text: A loose front connector on the radio.

feedback.text: No. The link light was steady; the connector was not the cause.

questiontext.text:
Read this BITE readout, then answer.

BITE REPORT — COMM RADIO No.2 — LRU 622-1140-001
SELF-TEST......... PASS
SOFTWARE BLOCK.... PASS  (P/N 285-A047 rev C, load L-2231)
RF SECTION........ PASS
FRONT PANEL....... PASS
FAULTS LOGGED..... 0

What does this readout tell the technician?

generalfeedback.text: Every line reads PASS and zero faults are logged, so the self-test is clean. A clean BITE is one of the conditions for a successful load; the technician can move on to the configuration report.

answer.text: The self-test passed with no faults.

feedback.text: Correct — all lines PASS and zero faults.

answer.text: The RF section failed the self-test badly.

feedback.text: No. The RF section line reads PASS.

answer.text: The software block is the wrong revision.

feedback.text: No. It shows P/N 285-A047 rev C, the correct software.

answer.text: There are faults still to clear first.

feedback.text: No. Faults logged reads 0.

questiontext.text:
Read this MEL entry, then decide.

MEL 23-11-01 — COMM RADIO No.2
Category: C (repair interval 10 days)
Provision: may be dispatched inoperative provided COMM No.1
is fully serviceable and the crew is advised.

Statement: Under this MEL entry the aircraft may fly with COMM No.2 inoperative for up to ten days, as long as COMM No.1 works.

True or false?

generalfeedback.text: A Category C item has a ten-day repair interval, and the provision allows dispatch if COMM No.1 is fully serviceable and the crew is advised. So the statement is true.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct. Category C = ten days, and the provision permits dispatch with COMM No.1 serviceable.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Re-read the entry: Category C gives a ten-day interval and the provision allows dispatch.

questiontext.text:
Read this work order, then answer.

WORK ORDER WO-4471 — STATION LINE 2
TASK: Load software L-2231 to COMM No.2 per SB 34-2231.
NOTE: Radios at hardware mod 3 are NOT eligible.
      Verify hardware standard BEFORE connecting the dataloader.

According to the work order, what must the technician do first?

generalfeedback.text: The note says "Verify hardware standard BEFORE connecting the dataloader", because mod 3 units are not eligible. Checking the mod comes before any connection.

answer.text: Verify the hardware standard of the radio.

feedback.text: Correct — the mod is checked before connecting.

answer.text: Connect the dataloader to the front connector.

feedback.text: No. The note says to verify the mod before connecting.

answer.text: Sign the tech log and close the job.

feedback.text: No. The tech log is signed after a verified load, not first.

answer.text: Fit a mod 3 card to the radio.

feedback.text: No. Mod 3 radios are not eligible for this load at all.

questiontext.text:
Read this IPC excerpt, then decide.

ILLUSTRATED PARTS CATALOGUE 34-52-11
FIG 03  ITEM 10  COMM RADIO ......... P/N 622-1140-001
        ITEM 10A HOLD-DOWN CLAMP .... P/N 622-1140-050
        ITEM 12  FRONT CONNECTOR .... P/N 622-1140-070

Statement: In this IPC, the comm radio itself is item 10 and its part number is 622-1140-001.

True or false?

generalfeedback.text: Item 10 in Figure 03 is the comm radio, P/N 622-1140-001 — the same LRU part number used throughout the unit. The statement is true.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct. Item 10 = the radio, P/N 622-1140-001.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Look again: item 10 is the comm radio and its part number is 622-1140-001.

questiontext.text:
Read this tech-log snippet, then answer.

TECH LOG — A/C 9
FAULT: COMM No.2 loses set frequency after power-up.
ACTION: Loaded L-2231 (P/N 285-A047 rev C). BITE green.
        Config report matches task card. Verification complete.
        No further faults found.  Signed: J. Ozols  08 AUG

What was done to clear the reported fault?

generalfeedback.text: The action line shows a software load (L-2231) followed by a green BITE and a matching configuration report — the full verified load. That is how the "loses frequency" fault was cleared.

answer.text: A verified software load of L-2231.

feedback.text: Correct — load L-2231, BITE green, config matched.

answer.text: A full replacement of the radio LRU.

feedback.text: No. The log records a software load, not an LRU change.

answer.text: A repair to the aircraft battery bus.

feedback.text: No. The action was a software load; the battery is not mentioned.

answer.text: A change to the front connector wiring.

feedback.text: No. No wiring change appears in the entry.

questiontext.text:
Join the two sentences into one, using the word in brackets.

The load finishes. Then run BITE. (once)

Write your full sentence.

generalfeedback.text: The time clause takes the present tense, not will: Once the load finishes, run BITE.

answer.text: Once the load finishes, run BITE.

feedback.text: Correct — present tense in the time clause.

answer.text: Once the load finishes run BITE.

feedback.text: Correct (add the comma after the time clause when you write it out).
Use: Once the load finishes, run BITE. No will in the time clause.

questiontext.text:
Join the two sentences into one, using the word in brackets.

The light turns green. Then press start. (when)

Write your full sentence.

generalfeedback.text: When the light turns green, press start. The trigger clause stays in the present.

answer.text: When the light turns green, press start.

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: When the light turns green press start.

feedback.text: Correct (remember the comma after the time clause).
Use: When the light turns green, press start. Not "will turn".

name.text: U3 · as soon as + present · transformation

questiontext.text:
Join the two sentences into one, using the words in brackets.

It starts. Then watch the bar. (as soon as)

Write your full sentence.

generalfeedback.text: As soon as it starts, watch the bar. Present tense after as soon as.

answer.text: As soon as it starts, watch the bar.

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: As soon as it starts watch the bar.

feedback.text: Correct (add the comma when writing it out).
Use: As soon as it starts, watch the bar.

questiontext.text:
Correct the underlined verb.

When the load will finish, verify the configuration.

Write only the corrected verb.

generalfeedback.text: English keeps the time clause in the present tense: finishes. Latvian and Russian mark the future in both clauses, which causes this common error.

answer.text: finishes

feedback.text: Correct — present tense, no will.
Use the present: finishes.

questiontext.text:
Add the missing word.

Once configuration is verified, close the job.

Write the two words that should replace the underlined word.

generalfeedback.text: English needs the definite article here: the configuration. Latvian and Russian have no articles, so learners often drop the.

answer.text: the configuration

feedback.text: Correct — put the article back.
Use: the configuration.

name.text: U6 · fix the dropped passive be

questiontext.text:
Rewrite the underlined part correctly.

Once loaded the software, run BITE.

Write the corrected part only (four words).

generalfeedback.text: Keep the subject and the passive be: the software is loaded. "Loaded the software" drops the verb be.

answer.text: the software is loaded

feedback.text: Correct — subject + is + loaded.
Use: the software is loaded.

questiontext.text:
Write the one bank term that fits the gap.

The screen showed a ________ error, which means the data was corrupted and could not be trusted.

generalfeedback.text: A checksum is a number that proves the data is not corrupted; a checksum error means the data cannot be trusted.

answer.text: checksum

feedback.text: Correct.
The term is: checksum.

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: data load = putting new software in; BITE = the unit's self-test; checksum = a number proving data is not corrupted; LRU = a box you can swap; dataloader = the tool that sends the software.

answer.text: the act of putting new software into a unit
the unit's own built-in self-test
a number that proves the data is not corrupted
a box you can swap on the aircraft
the tool that sends the software to the unit

questiontext.text: Match each term to the verb that goes with it.

generalfeedback.text: These are the collocations technicians use: run a BITE test, cross-check against the card, power cycle the unit, abort the load, confirm compatibility.

answer.text: run
cross-check
power cycle
abort
confirm

questiontext.text: Match each abbreviation to its meaning.

generalfeedback.text: LRU = line-replaceable unit; BITE = built-in test equipment; AMM = aircraft maintenance manual; SB = service bulletin; MEL = minimum equipment list.

answer.text: line-replaceable unit
built-in test equipment
aircraft maintenance manual
service bulletin
minimum equipment list

questiontext.text: Match each step of the load to its purpose.

generalfeedback.text: Each step has a job: the checksum proves the data; BITE checks the unit; the configuration report lists what runs; cross-checking confirms the fields; the tech log records the result.

answer.text: to prove the data is not corrupted
to let the unit test itself for faults
to see exactly what the unit is running
to confirm the report agrees with the card
to record the load and the result
